observations.observation: A slender brown shaft and silver spear point replace the first attempt's wrong short metal weapon. Upright and horizontal thrust poses retain the shaft and full point.

The low silver-gray cap and cheek guards match the qualified source family. The tall spike of the rejected first attempt is absent in the16 inspected poses; the separate spear point is not treated as a helmet spike.

Green short tunic, gray cuirass and shoulder pieces, red waist detail, brown sandals, blue rectangular shield with silver rim and gold boss/corners remain coherent. The generated shading and microgeometry are authored interpretations.

One stocky adult body, one head, attached limbs, continuous weapon grip and consistent facial identity are visible throughout. No duplicated or detached limb was observed; fine finger/toe microanatomy is not certified.

Real transparent alpha is present. No visible red/yellow fringe, cropped sandal or truncated spear point appears in the normalized contact sheets at native68/96 target heights. All16 alpha64 bounds remain inside their384x256 cells.

The initial normalization followed whichever foot was lowest and introduced a large lateral torso sweep. Centering the low zone containing both feet removes that artificial sweep. Small remaining stride motion is visible and acceptable for this coarse four-frame candidate. Ground contact differs by one source pixel between rows.

reviewedFrames.observation: Neutral guard: low cap, cheek guards, green tunic, blue/gold shield and separate upright spear remain legible.
Small head/hand variation; shield shape and warm skin palette remain consistent.
Raised chest/head pose keeps the same helmet, nose and equipment; no tall helmet spike.
Return to guard; both sandals and the complete spear point remain inside the cell.
Forward step with one planted sandal; the corrected lower-body pivot no longer pulls the torso far sideways.
Opposite leg lifts; the body scale, green garment and shield remain stable.
Alternate support pose; there are no duplicated legs or detached feet visible at the inspected scales.
Trailing sandal lifts into the next step; residual lateral motion is small and follows the stride.
Guard/anticipation begins with the spear held upright and the shield forward.
Spear lowers diagonally, with the grip and shaft connected to the weapon hand.
The arm extends into a horizontal thrust; the full spear tip is retained and no extra arm appears.
Recovery returns the spear upright without replacing its wooden shaft or shield.
Surprised open-mouth reaction retains helmet, spear and shield.
Backward lean and tilted shield read as recoil; the lifted foot remains attached.
Recovery pose keeps the same face, costume and weapon ownership.
Return toward guard; this is a coarse hit/recovery frame, not a complete canonical death animation.
